results.summary: There is no notify-the-seller API, so the 'Devralmak istiyorum' button was out of scope and I used the fallback. Each discover item now says the booking can only be taken over through the seller's link (discover.itemNote). The card also has a 'Devir nasıl çalışır?' <details> with 4 steps, and the property-title link that sent guests into the normal booking flow is now plain text.

SellPanel now lists only upcoming CONFIRMED bookings. Bookings with 48h or less to check-in are disabled options with the suffix '(girişe 48 saatten az; devredilemez)', and the default selection is the first transferable booking. When none are transferable, sell.none explains the 48h rule. The check uses an optional API field `transferable` when present and otherwise a 48h client default (crossOwner filed so the API can supply it).

The label is now 'Satış fiyatı ({currency})' / 'Your price ({currency})' and the hint shows the real maximum ('En fazla {max}'). Prices above the maximum are rejected in the browser with a field error (sell.askTooHigh) instead of a server round trip. The success message now gives the link's expiry (f.dateTime(res.expiresAt)) and says the booking moves to the buyer on payment and the amount is paid to the seller. The maximum is an optional API field `maxAskMinor`, falling back to totalPriceMinor (ratio 1).

The current code has no native pattern any more. The input uses parseAmountToMinor (accepts '1.500' and '1.500,00') and shows errors through the Field error prop (aria-invalid, focus moved to the field), and the hint already gives examples. I kept the examples in the new dynamic hint.

The submit button now reads 'Devir bağlantısı oluştur' / 'Create transfer link'. A note under the form (sell.keepNote, linked to the button via aria-describedby) says the booking stays with the seller until the buyer pays, and the price is paid out once the payment is approved.

Covered by the F913 and F909 changes: new button text and outcome note, a per-item note on how to take over, and the property link removed from discover items. The ambiguous 'son {expires}' is now 'son geçerlilik: {expires}' with date and time. The recommended '{original minus commission}' payout was not used because the code pays the full asking price (transfer-service payout = ask), so the copy says the amount is paid to the seller.

Added an in-page <nav aria-label='Bu sayfada'> at the top of TransferMarket, shown once the session is ready, with links to #sell (reuses sell.title), #discover ('İlanlara göz at') and, for signed-in users, #my-transfers. The signed-out login prompt now has id='sell' so that link still works. Section order is unchanged.

discover.terms now reads '… · son geçerlilik: {expires}' (EN: 'listing valid until {expires}'), and expires uses f.dateTime(item.expiresAt) so the time is shown. I did not do the optional <dl> restructure.
SellPanel shows the discover.loading text while /api/bookings is still loading (data === null && !error), the same as the other cards.

TransferMarket passes the session user's value through the helper emailVerifiedOf(user: SessionUser & { emailVerified?: boolean }). This compiles whether or not api-client's SessionUser has emailVerified yet; until /api/user/me returns it, it is simply undefined.

results.summary: Both functions now take a locale argument that defaults to DEFAULT_LOCALE: summarizeReviews(propertyId, locale) and generateReviewSummary(reviews, knownNames, locale). The route already calls summarizeReviews(id, resolveLocale(...)), and the existing callers (evals, the integration test) still work through the defaults.

apiFetch now applies AbortSignal.timeout when the caller passes no signal: 20 s by default, 45 s for payment, 3DS confirm, share/transfer pay and LLM endpoints, and 120 s for FormData uploads. The refresh call also gets a timeout. A new optional ApiFetchOptions.timeoutMs overrides it (0 disables). A timeout is thrown as ApiError(0, 'TIMEOUT', 'TIMEOUT'), and new exports isTimeoutError and TIMEOUT_CODE let callers detect it, so busy states now end instead of hanging. The payment-flow UI (keep the idempotency key, re-read status) and the useErrorText mapping belong to other owners and are listed in crossOwner. reset-password already catches network errors and returns to idle.

When a 401 is followed by a failed refresh, apiFetch dispatches window SESSION_EXPIRED_EVENT ('session-expired'). It does this only if this tab has seen a session (successful /api/user/me or refresh), so anonymous visitors never get it, and only once until the next login; logout() resets the flag. I created src/components/auth/SessionExpiredDialog.tsx: a native <dialog role=alertdialog> that clears the Header session cache and offers 'Giriş yap' (loginHref(), returns to the current page) and 'Bu sayfada kal' (restores focus). Mounting it in the layout, PropertyCard's 401 handling and the textarea drafts are listed in crossOwner. RoleGate already uses loginHref().

fetchCurrentUser now returns null only for 401, 403 or 404 and rethrows network, timeout and 5xx errors. useSessionUserCache (Header) already keeps the last known user when it rejects, so the Header part works now. ui.tsx useSession still has no catch: until its owner adds a status 'error' with a retry (crossOwner), RoleGate stays on 'loading' and an unhandled rejection is logged on such errors.

api-client no longer contains hard-coded Turkish user text: the default message for a non-JSON error body is now the neutral `HTTP ${status}`, and ApiError already carries status and code. useErrorText already maps errors with no code or a 5xx status to common.unexpectedError in every locale. The same Turkish default in src/lib/api-upload-progress.ts is listed in crossOwner.
The toApiError default message changed from `İstek başarısız (${res.status})` to `HTTP ${res.status}`. The matching test expectation is in testUpdates.

Same change as auth#1, done once: SessionUser.emailVerified is now typed, so ClaimForm and TransferMarket can read user.emailVerified directly.

results.summary: The location search now uses the shared normalizePlace helper, which ignores accents and Turkish İ/ı casing. It loads up to 1000 locations (LOCATION_SCAN_LIMIT), filters them in memory against the city/country name and the existing alias/district matches, and keeps the first 20. If the table holds more rows than that, it adds results from the old database `contains` query, removes duplicates and re-sorts. A 1-character query now matches cities starting with that letter, still ignoring accents (F1289). Empty q and the response shape { city, country }[] are unchanged, and the local fold() helper was replaced by normalizePlace.

The body is now checked with appealInputSchema before assertNoticeRateLimit(redis, client, "appeal") runs. Appeals get their own counter (key dsa:appeal:<client>), and a request that fails validation no longer uses up the limit. The doc comment was updated to match.

New fields added to the GET response, nothing removed: timeZone, checkInTime, a top-level cancellationPolicy ({ kind, version, rules }, defaulting to MODERATE when none is assigned) and a cancellationPolicy on every ratePlan. The rate-plan policy is chosen the same way booking-service picks it (non-refundable plan gives NON_REFUNDABLE, otherwise the plan's policy, otherwise the property's). If the rules cannot be read it is null. Checkout can pass these straight to freeCancellation(snapshot, { checkIn, timeZone, checkInTime }) from src/lib/booking/free-cancellation-deadline.ts.

bodySchema now accepts filtersOnly: z.boolean().optional(). When it is true, the route skips searchProperties and returns only { filters, ai_generated, llmMode, reason }. Without the flag the response is the same as before, with the same keys in the same order.

Created POST /api/transfers/claim/preview, which takes { token } in the body (z.string().min(20).max(1000)), returns previewClaim({ token, buyerId }), reports errors via toErrorResponse(error, "transfers.claimPreview") and exports dynamic = "force-dynamic". requireUser does not exist in the codebase, so it uses requireAuth, which still lets unverified users see the state. The contract test only checks that documented paths have route files, not the reverse, so it still passes without the entry (see notes).

If it exists, NoticeForm gets key={propertyId}, propertyId, a contentUrl built from the same base as dsa-appeal.ts (local appBaseUrl helper, since the dsa-appeal.ts one is not exported) and the property summary {title, city, imageUrl}. A missing listing renders <NoticeForm key="none" /> unlinked. If the DB query itself fails, the page falls back to the old behaviour (`<NoticeForm key={propertyId} propertyId={propertyId} />`, URL derived on the client).

Replaced the new-password <input type="password"> with <PasswordRevealInput id="password" ... className={authInputClass} />. PasswordRevealInput does not accept a ref, so inputRef was removed and the two focus-on-error calls now use a module-level focusPassword() (document.getElementById("password")). Per p032#0, the field now sits inside NewPasswordField instead of AuthField.

Added module-level noopSubscribe, clientSnapshot and serverSnapshot (same pattern as register/login) and `const hydrated = useSyncExternalStore(...)`. The submit button now has disabled={!hydrated} after the submitButtonProps spread.

Imported NewPasswordField and newPasswordOk, wrapped the password input in <NewPasswordField id="password" label value error>, deleted the local passwordOk in favour of newPasswordOk, and added the show-on-blur error like register. Dropped subtitle={t("reset.subtitle")} from AuthCard and removed the now-unused AuthField import.
The saving label on the submit button now uses t("reset.submitting"). The key already exists in messages/{tr,en}/auth.json.

The done view now shows the success text via AuthCard status={<Notice kind="success" live={false}>…</Notice>}. Because AuthCard stays mounted across the state change, its persistent role=status region announces the text. Added aria-busy={state === "saving" || undefined} to the <form>. focusTitle was already passed on both the done and invalidLink AuthCards.

Added signal: AbortSignal.timeout(RESET_TIMEOUT_MS) (20_000) to the /api/auth/password/reset fetch. A hung request now rejects into the existing .catch(() => null) branch, which shows reset.networkError and sets state back to idle.

A correct fix needs a new public per-room availability/restriction route plus service query (inventory + restrictions per room per day) and new booking keys, which is beyond a small crossOwner change.

ml-r074.notes:
Wiring that other owners still need to do:
1. src/app/booking/[id]/page.tsx (r015): read `booking.refund` from the GET /api/bookings/[id] response. It is null unless the booking is CANCELLED. Shape: { refundMinor, refundPercent, currency, status: REFUNDED|PENDING|NONE|NOT_CHARGED }. NOT_CHARGED means no card or credit was ever charged (HELD, RNPL or void). results.summary: minRating is now applied in structuralWhere (Prisma `ratingAvg: { gte }`, which covers both the substring and hybrid-ids catalog paths). The same check runs in the in-memory results loop next to minPrice/maxPrice, so total and paging stay correct even if the catalog cache is stale. It is also added to the catalog cache key, only when set, so existing keys don't change. The OpenAPI docs need no edit, because /api/search builds its parameters from SearchParamsSchema via queryParameters.

params.ts now imports MAX_SEARCH_GUESTS from @/lib/search/guest-limits, and `guests` uses `.max(MAX_SEARCH_GUESTS)`. The value is still 30 and there is no import cycle.

SupportChatInput now takes an optional `history` of `{ role: "user" | "assistant"; text }` turns (new exported type SupportChatTurn). History is trimmed, capped at 6 turns of 1000 chars, and a trailing copy of the current message is dropped. It goes to the LLM as a `<conversation_history>` block before `<user_message>`, with angle brackets neutralised, and the system prompt marks it as data, not instructions. For a short follow-up the current message is classified on its own; only if the intent is unknown is it re-classified with the last user turn, inheriting only informational intents (cancellation_quote/property_policy/booking_status) at capped medium confidence. Handoff signals still come only from the current message, so an earlier refund request does not re-open tickets. Earlier user turns (not assistant turns) also count as sources for the number check.

updateSupportTicketStatus now sets `resolvedById: status === "OPEN" ? null : adminId`; resolvedAt is still set only for RESOLVED. listSupportTickets selects resolvedById, and SupportTicketRow gains `resolvedById: string | null`. No schema change; the integration test assertion for RESOLVED still holds, and the OpenAPI list schema is not strict, so the extra field validates.

Added exported `previewClaim({ token, buyerId, now? })` and a `ClaimPreviewStatus` type. It takes no lock, makes no PSP call and does not touch attempt counters. It checks the feature flag like claimTransfer, then mirrors claimLocked: signature check → 'invalid', past exp → 'expired', then transfer lookup (missing / tokenHash / bookingId mismatch → 'invalid'), non-LISTED → 'gone', seller is buyer → 'self', otherwise 'ok' with expiresAt as an ISO string. One difference from the request: the token's signature is checked before it is decoded for the expiry check, so a forged token reports 'invalid' rather than 'expired'.
